name: Children's toothpaste
anchor: strictest sovereign finished-cosmetic technically-unavoidable-impurity limit on a total-content basis, with the swallowed-product (toothpaste) tier read across to the ingestion-adjacent oral forms and every adult-market loosening carve-out declined for a 0-5 product
native_basis: finished cosmetic product as placed on the market — total heavy-metal content per unit mass of the product as sold (ug/kg). Total content, never a migration or leachate number, never a colour-additive or raw-material purity specification, and never a dietary basis.
native_basis_label: finished cosmetic as placed on market (total content, ug/kg of product as sold)
scope_note: Dentifrices marketed for ages 0-5, fluoride and non-fluoride, including training pastes and gels. This is the swallowed form of the category: a 0-5 child has not reliably learned to spit, so a substantial fraction of each application is ingested, and that is precisely why Germany BVL 2017 and Washington State both write a dedicated toothpaste tier stricter than their general cosmetic limits. CROSS-CATEGORY BOUNDARY: Category 20 (Oral Care) carries the ADULT dentifrice row and both use the same toothpaste-tier instruments; this child row binds the same 0.5 mg/kg lead tier as the adult row and is therefore never the looser of the two, satisfying the Category 2 floor rule. Category 20 additionally carries mouthwash, whitening products and the non-formulation oral articles (toothbrushes, floss, irrigators, tongue cleaners, denture care); none of those is in scope here, and none of them is a cosmetic formulation to which a toothpaste ceiling could be stretched. INSTRUMENT-SCOPE NOTE: every numeric cell in this row names a TOOTHPASTE-SCOPED register row wherever one exists, so no scope stretching is required; only nickel, for which no sovereign publishes a toothpaste-scoped limit, is reached by a disclosed read-across.
basis_guard_note: Every named anchor must carry a FINISHED-COSMETIC basis. The guard exists to keep three foreign bases out of these cells: (1) the 21 CFR 73/74 colour-additive ingredient specifications, which are purity limits for one raw material (iron oxides, ultramarines, henna, bismuth citrate, talc-bearing pigments) and not a ceiling on the finished product; (2) the EU Toy Safety Directive 2009/48 and ASTM F963 element-MIGRATION limits, which measure what leaches out of an article and are numerically incomparable to a total-content limit; and (3) food maximum levels expressed as-consumed or on an edible-portion basis. A cell whose named anchor fails the guard resolves to a GAP and fails the build rather than shipping a conflated number. The toothpaste rows widen the guard by one phrase, 'product as sold', because that is the basis string Washington State's Toxic-Free Cosmetics Act uses for its statutory toothpaste lead limit; it is a finished-dentifrice total-content basis in the same family as the BVL cosmetic basis, not a migration or dietary basis.
method: HMTc Method v2.0 (government-limit default) as applied to a child-scoped cosmetic category: every numeric cell is the strictest applicable sovereign finished-cosmetic maximum in the row's native total-content basis, or a disclosed read-across of a stricter sovereign tier from the same instrument where that instrument writes an adult-market loosening carve-out that HMTc declines to adopt for a product marketed to ages 0-5. No cell is occurrence-derived.

Pb.basis: finished cosmetic as placed on market (total content, ug/kg of product as sold)
Pb.label: strictest applicable sovereign TOOTHPASTE lead limit (Germany BVL 2017 toothpaste tier)
Pb.substantiation: Two sovereigns publish a toothpaste-specific lead limit and both are named: Germany BVL 2017 at 0.5 mg/kg, which binds, and Washington State's Toxic-Free Cosmetics Act at 1.0 mg/kg, which is a STATUTORY limit and is named because it corroborates the existence of a dedicated swallowed-product tier from an independent legal system. Both instruments set toothpaste four to twenty times stricter than their own general cosmetic tiers, and the reason both give is the same: a dentifrice sits on the oral mucosa and is partly swallowed, more so in young children who have not reliably learned to spit. The child row is at least as strict as the Category 20 adult dentifrice row, which binds the same 0.5 mg/kg tier; the child row is never the looser of the two.

Cd.basis: finished cosmetic as placed on market (total content, ug/kg of product as sold)
Cd.label: Germany BVL 2017 toothpaste cadmium tier
Cd.substantiation: BVL 2017 publishes a dedicated toothpaste row for cadmium at 0.1 mg/kg. It is numerically identical to BVL's general cosmetic tier - BVL did not tighten cadmium for the swallowed form - and the toothpaste-scoped row is named rather than the general row so that no scope stretching is required to reach this product. Only BVL is named: Washington's Toxic-Free Cosmetics Act sets a toothpaste limit for lead only, and no other sovereign publishes a toothpaste-scoped cadmium ceiling.

tAs.basis: finished cosmetic as placed on market (total content, ug/kg of product as sold)
tAs.label: Germany BVL 2017 toothpaste total-arsenic tier
tAs.substantiation: BVL 2017 publishes a dedicated toothpaste row for total arsenic at 0.5 mg/kg, numerically identical to its general cosmetic tier. The toothpaste-scoped row is named so the cell rests on an instrument that regulates this exact form. Arsenic is reported as TOTAL arsenic; inorganic arsenic is controlled separately and cannot substitute.

iAs.rationale: No jurisdiction anywhere in the register speciates arsenic in a cosmetic product. Every sovereign cosmetic instrument - Germany BVL 2017, Health Canada, China NMPA 2015, Taiwan MOHW 2024, Korea MFDS, the ASEAN Cosmetic Directive and its national transpositions, India, Kenya, the EAEU - regulates arsenic as a TOTAL element, so there is no sovereign inorganic-arsenic cell for this or any adjacent cosmetic form. Nor is a near-neighbour read-across supportable: the only inorganic-arsenic maximum levels in the register are dietary (rice, fish oils, marine products), expressed on an as-consumed or whole-commodity food basis that is not comparable to a finished-cosmetic total-content basis, and importing one would be exactly the basis conflation this row's basis guard exists to prevent. Inorganic arsenic is nonetheless material rather than not-material in this category: arsenic in talc, mica, zinc oxide, titanium dioxide, iron oxides and clay-derived raw materials is predominantly inorganic, and mineral raw materials are present by design in four of this category's sixteen rows. The cell is therefore a control, not a not-material determination, and inorganic arsenic can never substitute for the total-arsenic cell.
iAs.reference_method: Speciated inorganic arsenic by HPLC-ICP-MS (EN 16802 or AOAC 2016.03, matrix-validated for the product form) on every certified lot, reported alongside the total-arsenic determination. No separate inorganic-arsenic ceiling is published; the lot is judged against the total-arsenic ceiling, which bounds inorganic arsenic by identity. ESCALATION: where inorganic arsenic is the majority of the reported total arsenic, or where the reported inorganic arsenic is above the manufacturer's trailing twelve-month distribution for the same form, the lot triggers mandatory raw-material traceback to the mineral or botanical component and a documented corrective-action plan before certification.

tHg.basis: finished cosmetic as placed on market (total content, ug/kg of product as sold)
tHg.label: Germany BVL 2017 toothpaste total-mercury tier
tHg.substantiation: BVL 2017 publishes a dedicated toothpaste row for mercury at 0.1 mg/kg, numerically identical to its general cosmetic tier and ten times stricter than the 1 mg/kg cluster (US FDA 21 CFR 700.13, Health Canada, Hong Kong, China, Taiwan) that governs general cosmetics. The toothpaste-scoped row is named because Korea and Health Canada expressly place therapeutic toothpaste outside cosmetic scope, so a general-cosmetic row would need a scope stretch this cell does not require.

MeHg.rationale: Methylmercury is a component of total mercury and cannot exceed it (MeHg <= tHg by identity), so the binding total-mercury ceiling on this row bounds it arithmetically. Methylmercury is produced by microbial methylation of inorganic mercury in anoxic aquatic and sediment systems and reaches humans by bioaccumulation through aquatic food chains. Neither the pathway nor the exposure route exists here: a finished dentifrice or lip product contains no anoxic aquatic compartment and no microbial methylating community; although this form is partly swallowed, the swallowed material is the cosmetic formulation itself and not an aquatic food-chain product. Mercury compounds are prohibited as cosmetic ingredients under EU Regulation 1223/2009 Annex II and are limited only as an unavoidable trace by the instruments named in the total-mercury cell, and every one of those instruments regulates mercury as a total element or as elemental mercury. No separate methylmercury ceiling is published; mercury on this row is governed entirely by the total-mercury cell.
MeHg.reference_method: No routine methylmercury determination is required. Total mercury is determined on every certified lot by microwave-assisted acid digestion with ICP-MS or by direct thermal-decomposition amalgamation atomic absorption, and the total-mercury ceiling bounds methylmercury by identity. RE-OPENING RULE: the applicability determination is re-opened, and methylmercury speciation (US EPA 1630 or an equivalent matrix-validated procedure) is performed, whenever the formulation declares a marine-derived raw material - algal or seaweed extract, marine collagen, fish or krill oil, marine-sourced squalane - since that is the only credible route by which organomercury could enter a cosmetic supply chain.
MeHg.substantiation: Speciation-bounded and matrix-justified. The determination is rebuttable and is re-opened by the marine-raw-material rule in the reference method; it is not a claim that mercury is absent, only that the organomercury species has no formation pathway or supply-chain entry point in this matrix and is bounded by the published total-mercury ceiling.
MeHg.regulatory_basis: No jurisdiction sets a methylmercury limit for a cosmetic product. Every sovereign cosmetic mercury instrument checked regulates mercury as a total element (or, in the US case, expressly as elemental mercury), because the cosmetic exposure route is dermal with incidental oral transfer and the cosmetic raw-material supply chain contains no organomercury source. The register's only methylmercury maximum levels are dietary limits on predator fish, tuna, shark, marlin, alfonsino and other marine animals, all on a fresh or frozen edible-portion food basis with no comparability to a finished cosmetic.
MeHg.jurisdictions_checked: Germany BVL 2017 Table 1 (technically avoidable heavy-metal contents in cosmetics); EU Regulation 1223/2009 Annexes II and III; US FDA 21 CFR 700.13; Washington State Toxic-Free Cosmetics Act; Health Canada Guidance on Heavy Metal Impurities in Cosmetics; China NMPA Safety and Technical Standards for Cosmetics 2015; Korea MFDS cosmetic trace-contaminant standards (2024 Notice No. 9 and the 2025 revision); Taiwan MOHW 2024; Hong Kong Cap. 640; ASEAN Cosmetic Directive 2019 and its Indonesian (BPOM 16/2024), Malaysian (NPRA 2022), Singaporean (HSA 2024) and Thai transpositions; India Cosmetics Rules 2020; Kenya KS 2937:2021; EAEU TR CU 009/2011; Sri Lanka SLS 187:2025 (draft, gated).

Ni.basis: finished cosmetic as placed on market (total content, ug/kg of product as sold)
Ni.source_scope: cosmetic products other than eye makeup or color makeup products
Ni.label: Korea MFDS non-colour-cosmetic nickel tier (10 ug/g), read across to dentifrice
Ni.substantiation: No sovereign publishes a nickel limit scoped to toothpaste. Korea MFDS is the only jurisdiction that limits nickel in a finished personal-care product at all, and in Korea a dentifrice is a quasi-drug rather than a cosmetic, so its 10 ug/g cosmetic tier does not reach this form by its own terms. It is read across, disclosed, as the nearest applicable sovereign nickel cell: the basis is identical (total nickel content in a finished topical product as placed on market), the EU treats toothpaste as a cosmetic product under Regulation 1223/2009 and BVL lists it in its cosmetic table, and the alternative would be to leave the analyte with no ceiling in the one row of this category that is routinely swallowed. The colour-cosmetic (30 ug/g) and eye-make-up (35 ug/g) tiers are not used.

Sn.rationale: No sovereign publishes a tin content limit for a finished cosmetic. The register's tin values are of two incompatible kinds. The food maximum levels (canned foods and beverages, 50-250 mg/kg) are dietary as-consumed limits set for tinplate migration into food and have no relationship to a topical product. The EU values are either Toy Safety Directive 2009/48 element-MIGRATION limits, which measure what leaches from an article under simulated mouthing and are numerically incomparable to a total-content number, or REACH entry 20, which caps ORGANOTIN species (dibutyltin and dioctyltin) at 0.1% in skin-contact and childcare articles and is a species limit, not a total-tin ceiling. Substituting any of these would be a basis or species conflation, so no number is published and the cell is a control.
Sn.reference_method: Total tin by microwave-assisted acid digestion and ICP-MS on the finished product, every certified lot. Result reported and trended lot over lot. Where the product carries a polymeric applicator, dispensing component or wipe substrate, that component is digested and analysed separately and is additionally screened for dibutyltin and dioctyltin by GC-MS against the EU REACH entry-20 0.1% article limit, which does apply to a skin-contact childcare article as an article limit even though it does not bind the cosmetic formulation. ESCALATION: any lot above the manufacturer's trailing twelve-month distribution for the same form, or any organotin detection on a polymeric component, triggers raw-material traceback and a documented corrective-action plan.

Al.rationale: No sovereign publishes an aluminium limit for a finished cosmetic. The only aluminium values in the register are EU Toy Safety Directive 2009/48 element-MIGRATION limits, a different basis entirely. The regulatory silence is not an oversight: aluminium is an INTENTIONALLY ADDED functional ingredient across this category - alumina is the standard surface coating on cosmetic-grade titanium dioxide and zinc oxide, aluminium starch octenylsuccinate is a routine powder and emulsion texturiser, and aluminium lakes are the standard insolubilised form of organic colourants - so no jurisdiction treats aluminium as a contaminant to be capped in a cosmetic. Because aluminium is present by design, a not-material determination would be false and an invented ceiling would be arbitrary; the cell is a control.
Al.reference_method: Total aluminium by microwave-assisted acid digestion and ICP-MS on the finished product, every certified lot. The applicant declares the intended functional aluminium contribution from named ingredients and its expected mass fraction; the measured total is reconciled against that declaration. ESCALATION: measured total aluminium materially above the declared functional contribution indicates an undeclared aluminium-bearing raw material or a contaminated mineral input and triggers raw-material traceback, ingredient-declaration review and a documented corrective-action plan before certification.

Cr.rationale: No sovereign publishes a total-chromium limit for a finished cosmetic. The three total-chromium values in the register (Mexico NOM-252 toy and school-article materials, Australia Customs 1956 toy coatings, ASTM F963 toys and children's articles, all at 60 mg/kg) are bioavailable-soluble MIGRATION limits on articles, not total-content limits on a cosmetic formulation, and reading one across would be the basis conflation this row's guard exists to prevent. Total chromium would in any case be a poor standalone ceiling: chromium in a cosmetic matrix is dominated by trivalent chromium, which is an essential trace element of low toxicity, so a total-chromium number would be non-protective against the species that actually matters. Total chromium is therefore controlled as a screening determination that gates the hexavalent-chromium cell, and no ceiling is published.
Cr.reference_method: Total chromium by microwave-assisted acid digestion and ICP-MS on the finished product, every certified lot. Reported as a screening total only and explicitly not as a health-protective ceiling. ESCALATION: any total-chromium result above the matrix-validated method reporting limit triggers mandatory hexavalent-chromium speciation on the same lot under the Cr(VI) cell's method; a total-chromium result above the manufacturer's trailing twelve-month distribution for the same form additionally triggers raw-material traceback to the pigment or mineral component.

Cr-VI.rationale: No sovereign publishes a hexavalent-chromium limit for a finished cosmetic. The only Cr(VI) value in the cosmetic instrument family is EU REACH Regulation 2020/2081 at 500 ug/kg, which is scoped to mixtures used for TATTOOING AND PERMANENT MAKE-UP - deposited intradermally, bypassing the skin barrier entirely - and is therefore a different exposure route, a different product class and a different risk basis; it is not read across onto a surface-applied children's cosmetic. The remaining Cr(VI) values are EU Toy Safety Directive 2009/48 element-migration limits on toy materials, a different basis again. A NOT-MATERIAL determination was considered and rejected for this category. The method-artifact argument - that Cr(VI) is reduced to Cr(III) in a reducing, organic, aqueous matrix - holds for some cosmetic forms but is not supportable category-wide here: although this row is a predominantly organic, aqueous or oleaginous matrix in which hexavalent chromium would be expected to reduce to trivalent chromium, the reduction rate in a low-water anhydrous or high-pH formulation is not established, mineral-derived fillers and colourants may still be present, and Category 2 is the child-scoped category where an unsubstantiated not-material claim carries the highest cost if it is wrong. Control is the correct fail-safe: testing is mandatory, the method and escalation rule are published, and no ceiling is fabricated.
Cr-VI.reference_method: Hexavalent chromium by alkaline digestion and ion chromatography with post-column derivatisation (US EPA 3060A with 7199, or an equivalent matrix-validated procedure), performed on every lot whose total-chromium screen is above the method reporting limit, and on every lot of a mineral- or pigment-bearing form regardless of the screen result. ESCALATION: any Cr(VI) detected above the matrix-validated method reporting limit triggers mandatory raw-material traceback to the pigment or mineral component, a supplier certificate of analysis for Cr(VI) on that raw material, and a documented corrective-action plan before the lot may be certified.
